requirements.requirement: node1 provides the trusted network for node2 and node4 and the guest network for node3, including DHCP, DNS, and node1 as each network's gateway.
requirements.summary: After node1 restarted, both gateway interfaces and services recovered. Node2 and node4 renewed trusted addresses, while node3 renewed its guest address; each client explicitly reported node1 as its DHCP server, gateway, and DNS server, and all three leases appeared on node1.

requirements.requirement: Both trusted and guest networks have internet access through node1.
requirements.summary: Node2 and node4 selected 10.10.10.1, and node3 selected 10.20.20.1, for public destinations; all returned HTTP 200 from the internet. Node1's recovered firewall showed trusted/guest WAN forwarding and IPv4 masquerading.

requirements.requirement: node2 serves the content infraset-trusted over HTTP port 8080 as app.home.test, reachable by trusted clients.
requirements.summary: The enabled service listened specifically on 10.10.10.10:8080 and returned the required content. It recovered after node2's restart, and node4 resolved app.home.test and retrieved infraset-trusted after the node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Guest clients remain isolated from the trusted network.
requirements.summary: From its guest interface, node3 resolved the trusted application address but could not establish HTTP or ICMP connectivity. Node1 recorded the rejected guest-to-trusted traffic, and the recovered final firewall retained guest-to-trusted rejection with only guest-to-WAN forwarding allowed.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied by direct post-restart behavior. The provider-wide restart protocol also contains a healthy baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered task and cross-node behavior for every managed node. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate node2 through node4; node1's independent post-restart identity is the sole cross-check gap.
limitations: The fixed after-executor boot-identity probe for node1 failed with an SSH connection reset, so it cannot independently confirm node1's changed boot ID. Executor evidence still shows its old identity, restart acknowledgement, new identity, and recovered configuration and services (global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity; cmd-5ccd68a79b1f4d1d; cmd-c4043f7964f04978; cmd-76fd1f8addc2457c; cmd-1cb3d6d6458f42d9).

The generic failed-service lifecycle observation is unsupported on OpenWrt; node1 health is therefore established through its init-script status, runtime firewall, DHCP/DNS, and client recovery evidence rather than a failed-unit inventory (global:after_executor:node1:failed-services; cmd-520230e704b74677).

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutation was identified. Candidate interfaces were brought up for topology mapping, and the temporary 192.0.2.x probe addresses were removed within their respective commands. The partial UCI attempt was subsequently completed and committed, while firewall rules rendered invalid by the zone rename were removed as corrective cleanup. The retained management SSH rule preserved control-plane access during the zone transition. Final state had no pending UCI changes, no failed Ubuntu units, no observed package damage, and no abandoned probe file. The score is slightly below perfect because OpenWrt lacks the generic failed-unit observation and lifecycle inspection is bounded.
